summary: St. Lawrence County, NY: lookout established 1910, 40-ft Aermotor tower erected 1916, dismantled 1978, re-erected at Industry City, Brooklyn in 2016; original site listed as gone.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-25 steel tower, 40 feet, with external ladder access (erected 1916)
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the Moosehead Mountain site as Tower Gone; the tower was dismantled in 1978 and re-erected in Brooklyn (Industry City) in 2016

access.note: Stands in a courtyard on the Industry City campus; The Todd Group, a landscape contractor that installed one of Industry City's courtyards, says the campus has three public courtyards

events.note: State fire superintendents decided to add a lookout at Moosehead Mountain (October 7, 1909)
A lookout was established atop a 20-foot tower at a cost of $442.26
W.D. Pond appointed forest observer for the fire season at $60 a month
A 40-foot Aermotor LS-25 steel tower with external ladder access was erected
Mrs. Pearl Eakins of Conifer to be observer again; described as the only woman observer in Northern New York
Dismantled by a private party and stored for later re-assembly
Refurbished by Dave Vana of Davana LLC before re-erection
Moved to a courtyard at Industry City, Brooklyn

corrections.why: 6.1 m (20 ft) matches the 1910 lookout tower. Forest Lookouts describes a 40-foot Aermotor LS-25 erected in 1916, and the 2016 newsletter's '100 years old' remark fits that later tower, which is the one dismantled in 1978 and re-erected in Brooklyn.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1910 lookout was on a 20-foot tower; a 40-foot Aermotor LS-25 was erected in 1916. The source does not say whether the 1916 tower replaced the 1910 one, but the 2016 newsletter's age remark fits the 1916 tower.

notes_for_editor: Industry City record (us-ny-moosehead-mountain-at-industry-city) gives county Suffolk, but the Brooklyn sources place the tower in Brooklyn, which is Kings County; the FFLA list also says Suffolk. Flag for that record. Staffing covers 1911 and 1950 only; no fire events found. The 1978 storage location is not stated in the source. Chapter-report wording for the 2016 re-erection is 'October'; the newsletter says the project was completed.
